title: The Unexpected Scholarship
premise: Jude Winterbourne, a scholarship student at elite Ashford Prep, hides behind an anonymous coding account that exposes the school's corruption—until he discovers his late grandmother's recipe box contains coded directions to a hidden inheritance tied to the town's founding families, including Ashford itself. As he deciphers the recipes, he's pulled into a decades-old cover-up of a stolen estate and finds an unlikely ally—and first love—in Priya Raman, the headmaster's daughter who is duty-bound to protect her family's name. When Jude's anonymous account is traced and the headmaster moves to destroy the evidence and expel him, Jude must choose between staying invisible and going public with the truth. In the end, he reveals himself, the inheritance is restored to its rightful heirs, and Jude learns that identity isn't something you hide—it's something you claim.
about_author: Emrys Sandoval is a former debate coach who grew up in a family of archivists and spent years cataloguing small-town estate records before turning to fiction. They write stories about quiet kids who discover that the past is never finished with them.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. We meet Jude navigating Ashford Prep as the invisible scholarship kid—perfect grades, closed locker, no friends who matter. At night, his anonymous account 'Winterlight' posts evidence of the school's rigged donor admissions. The beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. After his grandmother's funeral, Jude sorts her belongings and finds a recipe box where several cards contain no food at all—ciphers, coordinates, and a name he doesn't recognize: Ellery Vance. The emotional beat: grief cracking open into curiosity.

chapters.title: First Card, First Lie
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Deciphering the first card, Jude realizes the 'recipes' reference Ashford's founding documents—his grandmother knew the school's secrets. He cross-references the archive and finds a page physically cut out of the 1947 ledger. Beat: the thrill of being right, and afraid of it.

chapters.title: The Headmaster's Daughter
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya Raman, dutiful and exhausted, manages her father's image and catches a glimpse of Jude in the archive after hours. She covers for him without knowing why. Beat: two guarded people noticing each other across a locked door.

chapters.title: Winterlight Gets a Reply
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Someone responds to Jude's anonymous posts with a warning containing details only an insider would know. Meanwhile, the cut ledger page matches a recipe card. Beat: the game has noticed the player.

chapters.title: Detention with a Purpose
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, then Priya's. Jude is caught in the archive and sentenced to cataloguing duty—where Priya is assigned to supervise him. Their sparring over an old land deed turns into real collaboration. Beat: reluctant alliance, first spark.

chapters.title: Ellery Vance, Disappeared
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Research reveals Ellery Vance, a Black landowner whose estate was absorbed into Ashford's campus in 1948 through a forged sale. Jude's grandmother was the Vances' neighbor—maybe their ally. Beat: the personal becomes historical; justice has an address.

chapters.title: What Priya Knew
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers her father's office contains the missing ledger page and realizes the Raman name is entangled in the cover-up through an old endowment deal. Torn, she says nothing. Beat: love of family versus love of truth.

chapters.title: The Second Recipe
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A recipe card leads Jude and Priya to a sealed crawlspace beneath the chapel containing Vance's original deed and letters. Priya, holding evidence against her own father, hands it to Jude anyway. Beat: trust as an act of courage.

chapters.title: Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. After a near-discovery in the tunnels, Jude and Priya admit everything to each other—Winterlight is Jude; Priya has known for weeks. A first kiss in the dark, immediately shadowed by what they've risked. Beat: intimacy and exposure are the same thing.

chapters.title: The Trace
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The school's IT contractor, pressured by the headmaster, traces Winterlight to a library terminal and a timestamp. Jude realizes he has days, not months. Beat: paranoia tightening like a fist.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The final recipe card, baked into a loaf of bread per her instructions, reveals a letter: Grandma Ruth witnessed the forged sale as a girl and spent her life quietly gathering proof, leaving it to whoever was brave enough. Beat: inheritance redefined—courage passed down.

chapters.title: Vance Descendants
chapters.summary: Jude and Priya's POV, alternating. They locate Ellery Vance's great-granddaughter, Marisol Vance, a nurse in the next town who never knew why her family lost everything. She's hesitant—hope has cost her family before. Beat: the stakes acquire faces.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The headmaster privately offers Jude a full ride, a glowing recommendation, and silence about Winterlight—if the 'archive hobby' stops. Jude sees the trap: comfort in exchange for complicity. Beat: temptation wearing a kind face.

chapters.title: Priya's Choice
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Her father confronts her with the missing page and orders her loyalty. She lies to his face for the first time. Beat: duty inverted—she now owes her duty to the truth.

chapters.title: Locker Shut Forever
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The school raids Jude's locker and dorm, confiscating his laptop and expelling him pending a 'honor review.' The evidence seems gone—but Jude mailed copies to Marisol days ago. Beat: hitting bottom, secretly armed.

chapters.title: Winterlight Speaks
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Rather than stay anonymous, Jude posts his real name and the full story: scans of the deed, the forged signature, the letters. The post detonates across town. Beat: fear transformed into declaration.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the honor review, Priya walks in and testifies against her father, presenting the ledger page she stole back from his office. The room fractures; the board calls an emergency session. Beat: climax of conscience—love against duty, duty winning on truth's side.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The board, lawyers, and press converge. The forged sale is invalidated; Ashford's endowment is ordered to compensate the Vance estate. The headmaster resigns. Beat: justice outside the law finally enters the law.

chapters.title: Reinstated
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The expulsion is reversed, but Jude surprises everyone—including himself—by choosing to finish the year at his old public school, where he's needed and known. Beat: identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The House on Vance Lane
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Marisol reclaims the original Vance house; Priya, estranged from her father but at peace, visits Jude. They bake one of Grandma Ruth's real recipes together—actual food, finally. Beat: tenderness after the storm.

chapters.title: Signed, Jude Winterbourne
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At Marisol's housewarming, Jude donates Grandma Ruth's recipe box to the Vance family archive, keeping only one card—the bread. He signs his real name to a new post: no mask, no fear. Beat: full-circle resolution; the labels are off for good.
